A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TimeDART and retain matching core architecture and optimization objectives. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original forecasting experiments, pooled pre-training comparisons, ablations and hyperparameter analyses in Section 4 and Appendices C–F.

after.justification: v3 reports original forecasting and classification results, backbone comparisons and component analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The core autoregressive patch/diffusion pre-training procedure is retained. v3 adds a max-pooling classification head optimized with cross-entropy in Section 3.3 and evaluates a causal TCN encoder variant in Section 4.2. These are limited adaptations of the existing framework.

E1.justification: v3 retains the eight original forecasting datasets and adds four PEMS subsets containing five-minute traffic measurements, plus HAR, Epilepsy and EEG/Sleep-EDF classification tasks. Its pooled pre-training evaluation also expands from energy datasets to targets spanning energy, weather, finance and transportation.

E2.justification: The original forecasting comparator set is retained. v3 newly evaluates FormerTime for classification and adds SimMTM, self-supervised PatchTST, TimeMAE and CoST to the pooled pre-training comparison. That comparison previously contained only TimeDART and random-initialization variants, making the expanded comparison substantively stronger.

E3.justification: Pooled pre-training changes from five energy datasets to all forecasting datasets. New PEMS experiments use a 96-step input and 12–48-step horizons, with selected normalization omissions; classification introduces accuracy and F1 evaluation. v3 also reports native supervised baseline architectures instead of unified encoders and changes Traffic pre-training from 30 to 50 epochs. These reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds backbone substitution, decoder masking-ratio tests, independent versus common noise-step tests, and shared versus separate embedding comparisons (Tables 5, 14 and 17). Existing module ablations and sensitivity analyses are extended to PEMS and classification. ETTh2 is removed from the reported noise-step/scheduler sweep.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. Forecasting averages across prediction horizons remain aggregation across settings, rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive classification, PEMS, backbone and component results; HAR accuracy is reported as 0.9247 in Table 4. Some retained baseline scores change: CoST's Weather 96-step MSE changes from 0.216 in v2 Table 2 to 0.162 in v3 Table 9. Pooled pre-training results use changed conditions. Some averages change inconsistently: v3 Table 13 reports ETTm2 w/o AR MSE as 0.271 instead of v2's 0.281 despite unchanged constituent values.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a mean/variance derivation for same-step Gaussian corruption after instance normalization, motivating independent noise steps. Appendix C.1 adds representation-learning and classification task definitions. The original forecasting definition and diffusion/ELBO derivation are retained.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion broaden TimeDART from a forecasting-focused method to a representation-learning framework claiming effectiveness across forecasting and classification. The central contribution of combining global autoregressive modeling with local diffusion modeling remains.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands the mechanism argument around diffusion counteracting autoregressive overfitting to noise and anomalies. It adds interpretations of shared embeddings, redundant decoder context and TCN behavior, and attributes weaker Weather transfer to shared hyperparameters. v2's discussion of Exchange distribution mismatch and overfitting is removed.

D1.justification: v3 adds dataset split and input-size details for the new tasks, baseline repository links, and specifies that decoder parameters match the encoder except for depth. Reported RTX 4090 memory changes from 16 GB to 24 GB. Most original optimizer and hyperparameter information, and TimeDART's code-access information, are retained.

R1.justification: The broad forecasting survey is replaced by dedicated autoregressive representation-learning and time-series diffusion discussions. Newly cited works include CSDI, TimeDiff, AutoTimes and denoising autoregressive representation learning. This substantially changes the explanation of TimeDART's relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around representation learning, related work is reorganized, and the methodology is condensed and restructured. Task definitions move to the appendix, while implementation details and full results receive a substantially reorganized appendix structure.

P2.justification: The main text switches to two columns and adds a training overview, task-comparison scatterplot, masking diagram and classification/backbone tables. Architecture and sensitivity figures are revised. Detailed forecasting results move to Appendix H, with averages displayed in the main text; the existing forecasting showcases are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence for transferable representations and previously asserted design choices through classification, backbone substitution, and direct masking/noise/embedding controls. Adding competing self-supervised methods to pooled pre-training also improves validation. Reporting errors temper this gain: Table 13 introduces an incorrect ETTm2 ablation average of 0.271 where the listed values and v2 give 0.281. These errors reduce numerical reliability, but the broader validation and targeted component evidence provide a substantial overall improvement.
